turns.content: A prepared hexene/C7-aldehyde mixture elutes within 25 minutes in an isothermal 60-degrees-C GC run, but later chronological reaction-sample injections develop irregular small peaks that the first two lack. What does the prepared-mixture test establish, and what association is observed with cumulative injections?

The actual samples come from rhodium-catalysed hydroformylation of 1-hexene. What additional reaction-derived material could be present, and why might it challenge the low-temperature isothermal method?
Explain how retained high-boiling material could produce small peaks at changing retention times in later chromatograms even though the target analytes initially behaved well.
If retained material is the working diagnosis, what change to the GC program would directly clear it after the analytes elute?
State the selected procedure operationally, including any necessary instrument setting and what should happen before the next analytical run.
Calibrate this source and remedy as best supported rather than uniquely proven by the chronological observations.
Which blanks, standards, and controlled comparisons would distinguish column residue from continued vial reaction or an injector artifact?
Report the diagnosis, corrective procedure, and main validation checks.
